verdict.rationale: Copilot's own memory feature stores facts the user asks it to remember and uses them to make later responses more relevant. That is a first-party form of persistent, user-directed context. However, the evidence never documents a custom-instructions or preferences setting, and never shows memory shaping every response. Missing for 10: a dedicated custom instructions/preferences setting, documentation that stored preferences apply to all responses, controls for viewing and editing memory, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a power-user, I can set persistent custom instructions and preferences that shape every response

citations.quote: Copilot can store specific facts users request it to remember, allowing it to generate more relevant responses and suggestions based on that context.
Copilot may proactively generate personalized research suggestions for users based on things like past research queries and Copilot memory.
